Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

control verb and noun

hold back, restrain

also restrain, hold back, keep in check, self-control, lose control

classical

Ter. Haut. 919: nōn tū tē cohibēs?
Cic. Off. 2.18: mōtūs animī perturbātōs (Lewis & Short)

cohibeō, cohibēre, cohibuī, cohibitum

verb, second conjugation

hold back, restrain, keep in check

Of feelings, hands, oneself: īrās cohibēre (Verg. A. 12.314, Lewis & Short); ab aliēnō cohibēre manūs, keep one’s hands off other people’s things (Plaut. Trin. 1019).

Examples

  • nōn tū tē cohibēs? nōn tē respicis? … — prae īrācundiā, Menedēme, nōn sum apud mē.

    Won’t you control yourself? Won’t you think of yourself? … — I’m so angry, Menedemus, I’m beside myself.Ter. Haut. 919–921

  • īra furor brevis est; animum rege, quī nisi pāret, imperat

    anger is a short madness: control your temper, for unless it obeys, it gives the ordersHor. Ep. 1.2.62–63

  • moderāre animō, nē sīs cupidus

    control yourself, don’t be greedyPlaut. Mil. 1215

Other words

  • coërceō, coërcēre, coërcuī, coërcitum — keep in check, curb, discipline

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Tac. Agr. 4.4: nī prūdentia mātris incēnsum ac flagrantem animum coercuisset; Cic. de Or. 1.194: cupiditātēs (Lewis & Short); Traupman 150

    Of keeping people, animals or passions within bounds, by force if need be.

  • temperō, temperāre, temperāvī, temperātum — hold back, refrain

    verb, first conjugation; with the dative, or ā and the ablative · also used · classical · Plaut. Rud. 1254: linguae temperā; Verg. A. 2.8: temperet ā lacrimīs

    Sibi temperāre, to control oneself (Caes. BG 1.33, Lewis & Short); īrae temperāre, to keep one’s anger in check (Liv. 33.20.7, Lewis & Short).

  • moderor, moderārī, moderātus sum — keep within bounds, restrain

    verb, first conjugation, deponent; with the dative · also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 1215: moderāre animō, nē sīs cupidus; Hor. Ep. 1.2.59: quī nōn moderābitur īrae (Lewis & Short)

  • continentia, continentiae f. — self-control, restraint

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Inv. 2.164: continentia est, per quam cupiditās cōnsiliī gubernātiōne regitur (Lewis & Short); Traupman 150

    To lose control is nōn esse apud sē, to be beside oneself (Ter. Haut. 920–921).

See also calm down, keep one’s temper, control.
